title: Show HN: Open-Sourced Code Mode to Cut ~60% of My Rust Agent's Token Burn
description: For those who are tracking, Anthropic released an announcement last week about their experimental code mode for Claude Code, claiming some bonkers token savings when it comes to tool calls (95% on some workloads(1)). I haven't benchmarked it myself, but independent studies come in somewhere closer to 60~70% savings (2), but I digress. TLDR; I built an open-source version for the community. Context: I'm writing an AI RPG engine called Spookery, and I immediately wanted to try this technique for myself when I heard of it. Agent deployment is currently dominated by token costs, especially during tool calling (single prompt generating tens or hundreds of tool calls). Unfortunately, it looks like the only ones who are doing this seriously are big agentic products like Claude Code and Codex. So, I thought it'd be fun to try it myself and bring it to you all! The idea of Code Mode is simple but powerful. Instead of passing back tool call results back to the LLM one at a time, let the LLM batch calls by letting it write a short script using your tools.
